statement: A comment-and-string masker built for crediting evidence errs safely when it blanks too much: a hidden assertion only withholds credit. Reused under a reader that claims a universal, 'every test in this file is skipped', the same over-blanking hides the one counter-example and turns into a false assertion. A quote inside a regular-expression literal such as /['"]/ opens a string in that masker and can swallow a live test after it. Rules: before reusing a lexer under a claim of absence or universality, check which way its errors push; any doubt in the lexing (a quote or regular expression open at the end of its line, an unclosed comment) withholds the claim; and plant a control whose counter-example sits right after the construct the lexer misreads.
